questions.stem: The **Middle Ages** in Western Europe:

options.A: Covers the period from the fall of Western Roman Empire up to the 15th c.
options.B: Covers the period from the fall of Western Roman Empire up to the present.
options.E: A and C are Correct answers.

explanation_steps: The Middle Ages (Medieval period) began with the collapse of the Western Roman Empire in $$ 476 \text{ AD} $$ and lasted until the $$ 15^{th} $$ century. This era was defined by the **Feudal system**, where land was exchanged for military service and labor.

questions.stem: King in Kingdom Rwanda was known as;
explanation_steps: In the Kingdom of Rwanda, the monarch held the title of **Mwami**. This title was also used in the neighboring Kingdom of Burundi.

questions.stem: The **Opium war** was completed with the treaty of ____ in $$ 1842 $$ by.
explanation_steps: The First Opium War ($$ 1839–1842 $$) ended with the **Treaty of Nanking**. It was the first of the 'unequal treaties' and forced China to cede Hong Kong to Britain and open ports for trade.

questions.stem: English nobles rebelled against their **king John** to limit his power and forced him to sign a document in **1215** known as;
explanation_steps: The **Magna Carta** (Great Charter) was signed by King John of England in 1215. It established the principle that everyone, including the king, was subject to the law and guaranteed the rights of individuals.

questions.stem: Eritrean Patriot killed at the battle of **Halay** was in $$ 1894 $$ was;
explanation_steps: **Bahta Hagos**, the governor of Akkele Guzay, led an armed uprising against Italian colonial rule in December $$ 1894 $$. He was killed during the battle at Halay while fighting the Italian forces.

explanation_steps: While **Liaquat Ali Khan** was technically the first Prime Minister, **Mohammed Ali Jinnah** is the figure most associated with the leadership and founding of Pakistan in $$ 1947 $$ (serving as Governor-General). questions.stem: Emperor **Haile Silasie** was overthrown from power in $$ 1974 $$ due to;

options.A: Increase in Petrol price led to a strike by taxi drivers.
options.B: The sever defeat of Second Division of Ethiopian army in Eritrea.

explanation_steps: The downfall of Emperor Haile Selassie in $$ 1974 $$ was caused by a combination of internal factors: economic crisis (inflation and petrol price hikes), military unrest (mutinies and defeats in Eritrea), and widespread social protests by students, teachers, and workers.

questions.stem: The **reason** Kush civilization shifted their old capital **Napata** to **Meroe** was;

options.A: Availability of fertile soil and Timber wood
options.C: To protect frequent attack from Egyptians
options.D: Meroe was the center of trade

explanation_steps: The Kingdom of Kush moved its capital to Meroe around $$ 590 \text{ BCE} $$. Meroe offered better agricultural land, vast forests for timber (needed for smelting iron), was further from Egyptian military reach, and was strategically located for trade routes.

questions.stem: The following are **Primary sources** of History **except**;
explanation_steps: **Revised text books** are secondary sources because they are written by historians who interpret and analyze primary sources long after the events have occurred.

questions.stem: In Latin America the mixture of **Europeans** and **native Americans** were;
explanation_steps: **Mestizos** is a term used in Latin America to describe people of combined European and Indigenous American descent.

questions.stem: Pick out the **mismatched** one?

options.A: Pablo Picasso-------------introduced Cubism Painting Art style

explanation_steps: **Guglielmo Marconi** (or Nikola Tesla) is credited with the invention of the radio. **Thomas Edison** is famous for the light bulb, phonograph, and motion picture camera.

questions.stem: The following were **UN secretary generals** except;
explanation_steps: **Sir Eric Drummond** was the first Secretary-General of the **League of Nations** ($$ 1920–1933 $$), not the United Nations. The others listed served as UN Secretaries-General.

questions.stem: Which statement is **correct** about **Congo** in 1960s?

options.A: It was the Colony of Belgium until 1960.
options.B: Patrice Lumumba Pro-strong Central government was its 1st Prime minister.
options.C: Moise Tshombe was secessionist leader of the Katanga mineral wealth Province.
options.D: It disturbed by the Cold war and Foreign interventions.

explanation_steps: All statements are correct. Congo gained independence from Belgium in $$ 1960 $$, Lumumba was the first PM, Tshombe led the Katanga secession, and the country became a major Cold War flashpoint.

questions.stem: Which Derg’s offensive known as the “**Red Star Campaign**”?
explanation_steps: The **Sixth Offensive**, launched by the Derg in $$ 1982 $$, was officially named the 'Red Star Campaign' (Operation *Selahta*). It was a massive multi-front attempt to crush the EPLF in Nakfa and Sahil.

questions.stem: Identify the **wrong** pairing?
explanation_steps: All pairs are correct: The Umayyad Caliphate was based in Damascus, the Abbasids in Baghdad, the Fatimids in Cairo, and the early Islamic state under the Prophet and the Rashidun Caliphs was centered in Medina and Mecca.

questions.stem: At the top strata of **Aryan Caste system** in India were ;
explanation_steps: The **Brahmins** (priests and scholars) occupied the highest position in the traditional Hindu caste system (Varna).

questions.stem: Land granted to a **Vassal** in return for military service during the Middle Ages was;
explanation_steps: In the feudal system, a **fief** was the central element. It was a piece of land held by a vassal on condition of feudal service (usually military).

questions.stem: The following were members of **Axis powers** during WWII;
explanation_steps: The **Axis Powers** in World War II primarily consisted of **Germany**, **Italy**, and **Japan**. They fought against the Allied Powers (Britain, USA, USSR, France).

questions.stem: **Napoleon Bonaparte** was defeated by the combined forces of Britain and Prussia in $$ 1815 $$ at the battle of_______in Belgium.
explanation_steps: Napoleon's final defeat occurred at the **Battle of Waterloo** in June $$ 1815 $$. He was defeated by the Seventh Coalition, led by the Duke of Wellington and Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher.

questions.stem: Identify the **wrong** statement?

options.A: G. Abdel Nasser Nationalized Suez Canal in 1956 .
options.B: Cuban nationalist leader was Simon Bolivar
options.C: NATO was established in 1949 in Brussels.
options.D: The leader of Civil Right Movement in USA was Martin Luther King Jr.
options.E: First NAM conference was held in September 1961 in Belgrade, Serbia.

explanation_steps: **Simon Bolivar** was a $$ 19^{th} $$-century South American liberator. The nationalist leader of the Cuban Revolution was **Fidel Castro**.

questions.stem: First EPLF organizational congress was held in $$ 1977 $$ in **Fah** the secretary General elected was;
explanation_steps: During the First Organizational Congress of the EPLF in January $$ 1977 $$ at Fah, **Romodan Mohammed Nur** was elected as the Secretary-General, while Isaias Afwerki was elected as the Assistant Secretary-General.

questions.stem: **Sequence** refers to;

options.A: The relationship between cause and effect.
options.D: The facts on which history is based.

explanation_steps: In history, sequence is the order in which events happen. It involves placing historical occurrences in a chronological (successive) timeline.

questions.stem: The last Chinese dynasty overthrown by the revolution 1911 was;
explanation_steps: The **Manchu** (or Qing) Dynasty was the final imperial dynasty of China. It was overthrown during the Xinhai Revolution in 1911, leading to the establishment of the Republic of China.

questions.stem: The main **cause** forced America to join WWII in $$ 1941 $$ was;

options.B: Failure Policy of appeasement by Hitler.
options.C: Japan Kami Kaze Pilots attacked her naval base **Pearl Harbor** in Hawaii.
options.E: German submarines attacked US Ships in the Atlantic Ocean.

explanation_steps: The United States entered World War II after the Japanese surprise military strike against the naval base at **Pearl Harbor**, Hawaii, on December $$ 7, 1941 $$.

questions.stem: Allied forces launched military offensive during WWII to defeat the Axis powers in **north Africa in 1942**:
explanation_steps: **Operation Torch** was the British-American invasion of French North Africa during the Second World War, launched in November 1942.

questions.stem: Italian colonialism in Eritrea was witnessed by the following **except**;

options.B: Ruled the highlands by salaried chiefs the so -called Mislane
options.C: Limited education up to grade Four.
options.D: Discovered mining site areas in Eritrea.
options.E: They did not have any input in infrastructure.

explanation_steps: Statement E is incorrect because the Italians **did** invest heavily in infrastructure, including the railway from Massawa to Asmara, roads, and modern buildings in cities like Asmara (the 'Little Rome').

questions.stem: “**Back to Africa movement**” the idea of native Jamaican ;
explanation_steps: **Marcus Garvey**, a Jamaican political activist, founded the Universal Negro Improvement Association (UNIA) and advocated for the 'Back to Africa' movement to encourage people of African descent to return to their ancestral homelands.

questions.stem: Writer who familiarized **Nadow Ez** dismissal in $$ 1988 $$ as Eritrean **Dien Bien Phu**;
explanation_steps: Journalist and author **Dan Connell** famously compared the EPLF's decisive victory over the Derg's 'Nadew Command' ($$ Nadew Ez $$) at Afabet in $$ 1988 $$ to the battle of **Dien Bien Phu**, which ended French colonialism in Vietnam.

questions.stem: “**An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth**" policy of equal punishment was introduced in Mesopotamia by king;
explanation_steps: King **Hammurabi** of Babylon (reigned c. $$ 1792–1750 \text{ BCE} $$) is famous for his code of laws, which established the principle of *lex talionis* (the law of retaliation), often summarized as 'an eye for an eye'.

questions.stem: Ancient oldest civilizations were characterized by the following **except**;
explanation_steps: Most ancient civilizations (Mesopotamia, Egypt, Indus Valley, China) were **Polytheistic** (believing in many gods). Monotheism (belief in one god) was rare and only appeared later (e.g., with the Hebrews).

questions.stem: The **Architect** of Berlin Conference in $$ 1884/85 $$
explanation_steps: The Berlin Conference was organized by **Otto von Bismarck**, the first Chancellor of Germany, to regulate European colonization and trade in Africa.

questions.stem: **Leonardo Da Vinci** painting and famous masterpiece of the 15th c;
explanation_steps: The **Mona Lisa** is a half-length portrait painting by the Italian Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci that has been described as 'the best known, the most visited, the most written about, the most sung about, the most parodied work of art in the world'.

questions.stem: “From the point of view of justice, the opinions of the Eritrean people must receive consideration. Nevertheless, the strategic interest of the US in the Red Sea basin... make it necessary that the country has to be linked with our ally Ethiopia”. This speech was delivered by US Secretary of State;
explanation_steps: This famous and controversial speech was delivered by **John Foster Dulles** in $$ 1952 $$. It admitted that while justice favored Eritrean independence, US strategic interests favored linking Eritrea with Ethiopia.

explanation_steps: **Kwame Nkrumah** led the **Convention People's Party (CPP)** in Ghana. **TANU** (Tanganyika African National Union) was led by **Julius Nyerere** in Tanzania.

questions.stem: The leading city states of **ancient Greek** civilization were;
explanation_steps: Athens and Sparta were the two most powerful and influential city-states (poleis) in Ancient Greece. Athens was known for democracy and culture, while Sparta was known for its military prowess.

questions.stem: The term ‘**Maghreb States**’ collectively referred to;
explanation_steps: The **Maghreb** (meaning 'West' in Arabic) refers to the region of Northwest Africa, primarily including Algeria, Morocco, and Tunisia.

questions.stem: The head quarter of the **League of Nations** was:
explanation_steps: The League of Nations, established after WWI, had its headquarters in **Geneva**, Switzerland, because of Switzerland's neutrality.

questions.stem: American war of independence was **successful** in the following **except**:
explanation_steps: The American Revolution did **not** immediately abolish slavery. Slavery continued in the United States until the end of the American Civil War in 1865.

questions.stem: Italians encouraged **Fruit and Vegetables** plantation in;
explanation_steps: **Ela Bered** (De Nadai estate) was one of the most famous Italian agricultural concessions in Eritrea, specializing in the large-scale production of fruits and vegetables for export.

questions.stem: In $$ 1958 $$ **Mao** launched a radical progame, to speed up an economic growth known as;
explanation_steps: The **Great Leap Forward** ($$ 1958–1962 $$) was an economic and social campaign by the Communist Party of China aimed at rapidly transforming the country from an agrarian economy into a socialist society through rapid industrialization and collectivization.

questions.stem: The commander of the **Barka** area during Sector commands was;
explanation_steps: In $$ 1965 $$, the ELF divided Eritrea into five military sectors. **Omer Ezaz** was appointed as the commander of the **Second Sector** (Barka area).

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** among the achievements of Chinese civilization?
explanation_steps: Pyramid building is a major achievement of the **Ancient Egyptian** civilization, not China. China's contributions include paper, printing, silk, and acupuncture.

questions.stem: European Explorer who discovered **Victoria Falls** was;
explanation_steps: **David Livingstone**, a Scottish missionary and explorer, was the first European to see Victoria Falls in 1855, naming them after Queen Victoria.

questions.stem: Identify the **wrong** Pairing
explanation_steps: All pairings are correct: Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire, Akbar was a great ruler of the Mughal Empire in India, Ashoka was the greatest ruler of the Mauryan Empire, and Sundiata Keita founded the Mali Empire.

questions.stem: The following were **Utopian Socialism** leaders **except** ;
explanation_steps: **Karl Marx** is the founder of **Scientific Socialism** (Marxism). He criticized Utopian Socialists (like Saint-Simon, Owen, and Fourier) for being unrealistic and not understanding the class struggle.

questions.stem: Movement in Sudan aimed to expel foreign rule and restore Islamic tradition was;
explanation_steps: The **Mahdist War** ($$ 1881–1899 $$) was an Islamic revolt led by Muhammad Ahmad (the Mahdi) against the Turco-Egyptian administration and later the British in Sudan.

questions.stem: The following Eritrean towns were remained **Under enemy control** in $$ 1977 $$ **except**;
explanation_steps: In $$ 1977 $$, the Eritrean liberation fronts (EPLF and ELF) liberated almost all of Eritrea. **Keren** was liberated in July $$ 1977 $$. Towns like Asmara, Barentu, Adi Keih, and Assab remained under Ethiopian (Derg) control.

questions.stem: The new leadership **Kiada -al- Amma** was product of___in $$ 1969 $$.
explanation_steps: The **Adobha Conference** ($$ 1969 $$) was held to resolve internal crises within the ELF. It resulted in the dissolution of the Sector system and the creation of a temporary unified leadership called **Kiada al-Amma** (General Command).

questions.stem: The **wealthy** class during the imperial Japan were known as ;
explanation_steps: In feudal Japan, the **Daimyo** were powerful land-holding magnates or territorial lords who were the wealthy elite. They subordinate only to the Shogun.

questions.stem: Identify the European explorer who **reached Indian soil in 1497**;
explanation_steps: **Vasco da Gama** set sail from Portugal in 1497 and became the first European to reach India by sea, arriving in Calicut in May 1498.

explanation_steps: During the Russian Revolution of 1917, Lenin and the Bolsheviks used the slogan "**Peace, Land, and Bread**" to appeal to the war-weary soldiers, landless peasants, and starving urban workers.

questions.stem: Newly independent African nations were affected in 1960s by;
explanation_steps: After gaining independence in the 1960s, many African nations faced multiple challenges, including political instability (coups), the rise of authoritarian one-party states, border disputes inherited from colonialism, and severe economic struggles.

questions.stem: People began **agriculture** and started to live in communities and engaged in **Animal domestication** in____age.
explanation_steps: The **Neolithic Age** (New Stone Age) is defined by the transition from hunting and gathering to farming (agriculture) and the domestication of animals.

questions.stem: The agreement signed in $$ 1904 $$ b/n **France** and **Britain** to solve their colonial disputes in Africa was;
explanation_steps: The **Entente Cordiale** was a series of agreements signed in $$ 1904 $$ between Britain and France, which settled outstanding colonial disputes and paved the way for their alliance in WWI.

questions.stem: One of the following favored the formation of homeland for Jews in Palestine from 1917 onwards.
explanation_steps: The **Balfour Declaration** (1917) was a public statement issued by the British government during WWI announcing support for the establishment of a "national home for the Jewish people" in Palestine.

questions.stem: The Chinese leader who was known for his policy **Four Modernization** focused on Trade, Industry, Technology and National defense was;
explanation_steps: **Deng Xiaoping** introduced the 'Four Modernizations' in the late 1970s to strengthen China's economy. This policy marked China's transition toward a more market-oriented economy.

questions.stem: The **first** Eritrean town to be liberated in January $$ 1977 $$ was;
explanation_steps: **Karora**, located on the border with Sudan, was the first town to be liberated by the EPLF in January $$ 1977 $$, marking the beginning of a series of victories that year.

questions.stem: **July, 1978** in the Eritrean History:

options.A: Wuqaw Ez(command)was crushed in northeastern Sahil.
options.C: EPLF conducted Strategic withdrawal due to Soviet massive support for Derg.
options.D: Second national and unity congress of EPLF held.
options.E: Demise of ELF by the EPLF.

explanation_steps: In **July $$ 1978 $$**, following the massive intervention of the Soviet Union on the side of the Derg, the EPLF decided to conduct a **Strategic Withdrawal** from the liberated towns to the base areas in Sahil to preserve its forces.

questions.stem: The Empire of **Monomotapa** was in Zimbabwe was built up by,
explanation_steps: The Kingdom of Mutapa (Monomotapa) was a medieval African empire established by the **Shona** people in the region of modern-day Zimbabwe and Mozambique.

questions.stem: The UN Organization that deals with **Refugee** Affairs;
explanation_steps: **UNHCR** stands for the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees. It is the UN agency mandated to aid and protect refugees.

- ELM defeated at Ella Tsaeda: **1965** (This was the final blow to the ELM by the ELF).

questions.stem: The following were **Asian Tigers** countries except;
explanation_steps: The **Four Asian Tigers** are South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, and Hong Kong. They are known for their rapid industrialization and high economic growth rates between the 1960s and 1990s. **Vietnam** was not part of this original group.

questions.stem: The **splinter group** severely attacked by **Kiada al Amma** was;
explanation_steps: The **Kiada al-Amma** (General Command) of the ELF sought to suppress splinter groups that emerged in the early 1970s. The **Obel (Ubel)** group was one of the primary targets of these internal military attacks before the groups eventually merged to form the EPLF.

questions.stem: Special envoy sent by the UN to supervise the **Eritrean referendum** in $$ 1993 $$ was;
explanation_steps: **Samir Sambar** was the UN Special Representative for the Establishment of the United Nations Observer Mission to Verify the Referendum in Eritrea (UNOVER) in $$ 1993 $$.

questions.stem: The Treaty signed on 25th Oct, 1896 after battle of Adwa was **_________________**.
explanation_steps: The **Treaty of Addis Ababa**, signed on October 26, 1896, formally ended the First Italo-Ethiopian War. It saw Italy recognize the absolute independence of Ethiopia and annulled the Treaty of Wuchale.

questions.stem: Match the item from Column A: **Osman Salih Sabbe**
explanation_steps: **Osman Salih Sabbe** was a prominent political leader in the Eritrean liberation struggle who led the **ELF Foreign Mission** and later founded the ELF-PLF.

questions.stem: Autocratic Ugandan President Milton Obote was overthrown by Military Coup in 1971 led by General **_____________**.
explanation_steps: In January 1971, while President Milton Obote was attending a Commonwealth summit in Singapore, **General Idi Amin** seized power in a military coup, beginning an eight-year period of brutal dictatorship in Uganda.

questions.stem: Match the item from Column A: **Colons**
explanation_steps: The term **Colons** refers to the European (predominantly French) settlers who lived in Algeria during the period of French colonial rule.

questions.stem: Scottish Engineer invented Steam engine in 1769 was **___________**.
explanation_steps: While Thomas Newcomen invented the first atmospheric steam engine, it was the Scottish engineer **James Watt** who patented a much more efficient version with a separate condenser in 1769, which powered the Industrial Revolution.

questions.stem: Match the item from Column A: **Raesi Tesema Asberom**
explanation_steps: **Raesi Tesema Asberom** was a leading Eritrean political figure and the founder of the **Liberal Progressive Party (LPP)**, which advocated for Eritrean independence.

questions.stem: The first Sub-Saharan country won its independence in 1957 was **__________**.
explanation_steps: On March 6, 1957, the British colony of the Gold Coast became the independent nation of **Ghana**, led by Kwame Nkrumah. It was the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to gain independence from European colonial rule.

questions.stem: Match the item from Column A: **Ahran Drup**
explanation_steps: **Colonel Arrendrup** (Ahran Drup) was a Danish officer hired by the Khedive of Egypt to lead an expedition against Ethiopia. He was killed at the **Battle of Gundet** in 1875.

questions.stem: The First Commando raid on the Asmara air port resulted 33 enemy helicopters burned took place in the year **______**.
explanation_steps: On the night of May 20-21, **1984**, EPLF commandos carried out a spectacular raid on the Ethiopian airbase in Asmara (Yohannes IV airport), destroying or damaging over 30 aircraft (including helicopters and MiGs) in less than 20 minutes.

questions.stem: Match the item from Column A: **Long March**
explanation_steps: The **Long March** was a massive military retreat undertaken by the Red Army of the Communist Party of **China** to evade the pursuit of the Kuomintang (Nationalist) army.
